subject: Pre-deploy: node fleet sizing, disk quota & KV cache persistence agreement
messages:
From: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@groundforge.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: ops@groundforge.com, amy.legal@groundforge.com
Date: Sat, 28 Jul 2028 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem prep: disk quotas, node mix and KV cache durability questions

Diego / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We want to lock the acceptance criteria for the on-prem cluster so our PM and procurement teams can finish the SOW. Two quick, concrete asks from Ops and Security: 

1) Disk quotas: we need a clear guidance table for node roles (worker-gpu, worker-general, system) that spells out persistent volume classes, expected per-pod quota, and eviction thresholds. Our infra team wants to know whether local NVMe will be used for ephemeral cache or if you recommend blockstore-backed cache with explicit eviction windows.

2) KV cache persistence: during node restarts and upgrades we need to understand whether model KV cache warmup will be tolerated or if Redwood can provide a warm-start snapshot workflow (and the size/transfer profile). If the KV cache is large, we need a fallback policy so tail latency doesn't spike on 99th percentile during canary rollouts.

3) Rollout acceptance: can you confirm the checklist items your SRE will validate on day 0 (networking, anti-affinity, PVC attachment, KMS access)? We'll need that list for sign-off.

I'm attaching our internal intake (ops inventory) but it's still light on node sizing — can you send a recommended node-fleet spreadsheet and a short runbook we can include in the SOW?

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

—Liam
Liam O'Neal
Head of Infrastructure, GroundForge Systems
liam.oneal@groundforge.com
+1 415-555-0193

Attachments: ops-inventory-template.xlsx (stub)

From: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@groundforge.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com, Amy Park <amy.legal@groundforge.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Jul 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem prep: disk quotas, node mix and KV cache durability questions

Liam — thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front and a proposed delivery plan below. See attached draft sizing workbook and our predeploy checklist PDF.

Disk quotas / node roles (summary):
- worker-gpu: reserved for heavy model inferencing. Recommend 2 x 2TB NVMe per node for local KV caching + 100Gi PV class for logs/metrics. Eviction threshold: 85% local usage, 90% triggers pod eviction policy.
- worker-general: mixed traffic for routing + small models. 1 x 1TB NVMe per node, 50Gi PV class. Eviction threshold: 80%.
- control/system: small fleet (3 control-plane VMs) with 500Gi blockstore for backups/etcd snapshots. Node anti-affinity required across racks.

KV cache persistence policy:
- Option A (recommended): local NVMe-backed KV cache with periodic warm-state snapshotting to blockstore. Snapshots are incremental; typical transfer on restore for a 30B model KV is ~1.2GB (metadata + partial layers). Restore during autoscaling/canary uses snapshot + lazy-fill to avoid high tail latency.
- Option B: blockstore-only warm start (slower network restore but simpler for air-gapped sites).

Rollout acceptance checklist (day 0 highlights):
- BGP/VPC routing validated (control plane reachability across racks)
- KMS integration tested using a sample key (rotate/read)
- PVC attach/detach stress test (3x attach cycles per PV class)
- Node-level eviction simulated at 82% and 91% to verify SLOs
- KV cache restore on a canary node and 10% traffic soak for 30m

Delivery plan:
- Today (EOD): share spreadsheet and checklist (attached).
- Mon: SRE/field-eng workshop (1h) to walk the checklist and confirm eviction thresholds with your infra.
- Wed: run small attach/eviction trial in your staging rack with our on-site engineer.

CC'd Neha (security/compliance owner) for KMS and audit-log evidence and Marissa (customer ops) for runbook handoff. Jordan will coordinate the on-site schedule and provide a final BOM.

If the above looks good, we'll finalize the SOW language around node-count elasticity and KV snapshot SLAs.

—Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.com

Attachments: sprint0-nodefleet-sizing.xlsx (draft), redwood-k8s-predeploy-checklist.pdf

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@groundforge.com>, diego.fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com, Amy Park <amy.legal@groundforge.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Jul 2028 13:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem prep: disk quotas, node mix and KV cache durability questions

Liam — quick note from security side: two items to confirm before we sign-off on day 0.

1) KMS escrow: we need a documented key-handoff process for emergency access (paper trail + pre-authorized break-glass) and a SOC-style attestation that your KMS operator list is final. Please add your KMS admin alias to the intake doc.

2) Audit trail for KV snapshot transfers: if you choose Option A (NVMe local + snapshot to blockstore), snapshots are encrypted in transit and at rest. We will provide an evidence package (screenshot + signed manifest) after the first snapshot job runs. That package will be attached to the SOW as Appendix A.

One caveat on eviction thresholds: we recommend a staggered evacuation policy for GPU nodes (drain with prioritized pod migration) rather than immediate eviction. Diego's suggested thresholds are fine, but ops should accept a 15-30m graceful drain window for model state replication.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

From: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@groundforge.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com, Amy Park <amy.legal@groundforge.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Jul 2028 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem prep: disk quotas, node mix and KV cache durability questions

Thanks — that all helps. Couple of clarifications before the Mon workshop: 

- On the NVMe snapshot size: can you call out the expected restore time over a 10Gb interconnect vs a 1Gb fallback? We have two potential racks with different uplinks.
- For the SOW, procurement needs the exact spare-part list (we need to know how many spare NVMe drives per rack you expect for the recommended node counts). Jordan — can you confirm your proposed dates for the on-site trial?

We'll review the draft spreadsheet and comment inline. Amy (legal) — if we accept the Appendix A attestation, we still need a short clause that limits Redwood's liability for snapshot transit (standard).

Appreciate the tight coordination. I'll have our infra team add the KMS admin alias to the inventory doc tonight.

—Liam

Thread notes: attachments referenced (sprint0-nodefleet-sizing.xlsx, redwood-k8s-predeploy-checklist.pdf). Internal action items: set Mon workshop (Diego/Jordan), produce spare-part list (Jordan), provide 10Gb vs 1Gb restore estimates (Diego), finalize Appendix A language (Neha + Amy).
